title: Coherent naive cotangent cohomology over a locally Noetherian base
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Suppose $Y$ is locally Noetherian, meaning it admits a surjective etale cover by schemes with affine open covers by spectra of Noetherian rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Suppose $f$ is locally of finite presentation, tested on etale scheme charts [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Then $X$ is locally Noetherian, $\mathcal O_X$ is coherent, and $\mathrm{NL}_{X/Y}$ [def-sfb-space-naive-cotangent-complex] has coherent cohomology sheaves, zero outside degrees $-1,0$. Coherent here means that on every Noetherian affine etale chart the module sheaf is associated to a finitely generated module; association on an affine chart $\operatorname{Spec}R$ sends a module $N$ to the etale sheaf with value $B\otimes_RN$ on affine etale charts $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}R$. Thus $\mathrm{NL}_{X/Y}$ and $\mathcal O_X[0]$ belong to $D^b_{\mathrm{Coh}}(\mathcal O_X)$, the full subcategory of $D(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] consisting of complexes with coherent cohomology vanishing in all but finitely many degrees.

proof.text: Choose a locally Noetherian scheme atlas $V\to Y$ and any scheme atlas $U_0\to X$. The fibre product $U=U_0\times_YV$ is a scheme by representability of the diagonal of $Y$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. The projection $U\to U_0$ is surjective etale, hence $U\to X$ is a surjective etale chart. The induced scheme map $U\to V$ is locally of finite presentation by the chart hypothesis [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Finite algebra presentations give finite generating sets, so it is locally of finite type. Apply [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft] to $U\to V$: $U$ is locally Noetherian. Its surjective etale map to $X$ proves that $X$ is locally Noetherian in precisely the sense of the statement.

Take the cover and derived isomorphisms in [lem-sfb-space-naive-cotangent-finite-local-model]. Refine its charts $U_i$ by $U_i\times_XU$, with $U$ from step 1. These are schemes by the representable diagonal of $X$, and they are etale over the locally Noetherian scheme $U$. An etale scheme map is locally of finite presentation [def-weil-etale-morphism], hence locally of finite type; [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft] makes each refined chart locally Noetherian. Refine further by Noetherian affine opens $W=\operatorname{Spec}R$. Restriction to a chart is localization of the small etale site and is exact by [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact], so its degreewise application commutes with kernels, cokernels and cohomology. It therefore takes quasi-isomorphisms to quasi-isomorphisms and induces restriction on the derived localization [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], preserving the displayed derived isomorphisms. It also restricts local presentations. On $W$ the model is still $[F^{-1}\xrightarrow d F^0]$ with the stated finiteness. Its cohomology is $\ker d$ in degree $-1$, $\operatorname{coker}d$ in degree $0$, and zero elsewhere.

source.place: Tag 0D0Z, lemma-netherlander-fp; restriction and two-term cohomology.

proof.text: Use [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence] to write these terms as $A_W(G^{-1})$ and $A_W(G^0)$ and the differential as $A_W(e)$. The finite presentation of $F^0$ includes a finite free epimorphism, so both terms are of finite type. By [lem-sfb-scheme-etale-module-exact-finiteness-comparison], $G^{-1}$ and $G^0$ are finite-type Zariski quasi-coherent modules and this comparison is exact in ambient module sheaves. By [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-finite-type-affine], their section modules $M^{-1},M^0$ over $R$ are finitely generated. The unit and counit of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction] identify $G^j=\widetilde{M^j}$ and $e=\widetilde v$ for an $R$-linear map $v:M^{-1}\to M^0$. The associated-sheaf functor preserves kernels by [lem-sc-tilde-preserves-finite-limits] and cokernels by the colimit clause of that adjunction. Exactness of $A_W$ therefore identifies the two cohomology sheaves with $A_W(\widetilde{\ker v})$ and $A_W(\widetilde{\operatorname{coker}v})$.

source.place: Tags 03DX, 06VE (5), 05VG; affine module comparison and exact associated sheaves.

proof.text: Since $R$ is Noetherian and $M^{-1}$ is finitely generated, [lem-trf-noetherian-submodule-finitely-presented] gives finite generation of $\ker v$. Images in $\operatorname{coker}v$ of any finite generating set of $M^0$ generate that quotient. Thus both cohomology sheaves on $W$ are quasi-coherent and of finite type by the affine criterion and the finiteness comparison cited in step 3. This is the only place Noetherianness is needed for the kernel; no projectivity of differentials or regularity of $f$ has been assumed.

The finite-type and quasi-coherent conclusions glue as site-local properties: for an arbitrary chart $T\to X$, pull back the covering charts $W\to X$, and then use their local presentations. Composing covering families gives local presentations on $T$; this is exactly the quasi-coherent predicate [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module] and the finite-type predicate in the local-model statement. Exact chart restriction from step 2 identifies these restrictions with the cohomology of $\mathrm{NL}_{X/Y}$. Let $u:T=\operatorname{Spec}R'\to X$ be any Noetherian affine etale chart and $H$ one of these cohomology sheaves. By [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence], $H|_{T_{\mathrm{et}}}\simeq A_T(G)$ for a quasi-coherent Zariski module $G$; by [lem-sfb-scheme-etale-module-exact-finiteness-comparison] $G$ is of finite type, so $N=G(T)$ is a finitely generated $R'$-module by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-finite-type-affine], and $G\simeq\widetilde N$ by the counit of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction]. For an affine etale chart $a:\operatorname{Spec}B\to T$, [lem-sc-affine-top-tensor-sections] gives $A_T(\widetilde N)(\operatorname{Spec}B)=\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}B,a^*\widetilde N)\simeq N\otimes_{R'}B$. This is association to a finitely generated module, exactly the stipulated meaning of coherent. Vanishing outside $-1,0$ also follows from the two-term definition [def-sfb-space-naive-cotangent-complex].

source.place: section-properties-modules, site-local properties (j),(k); etale covering transitivity.

proof.text: On a Noetherian affine chart $\operatorname{Spec}R$, the structure sheaf of [def-trf-algebraic-space] is the sheaf associated to the cyclic module $R$ by the formula $B\otimes_RR=B$. Hence $\mathcal O_X$ is coherent in the stated sense. The only cohomology of $\mathcal O_X[0]$ is this sheaf in degree zero, and the only possible nonzero cohomology of $\mathrm{NL}_{X/Y}$ is the coherent cohomology in degrees $-1,0$ proved above. Both objects therefore satisfy the definition of $D^b_{\mathrm{Coh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ given in the statement.

lean.statement: theorem naiveCotangent_coherent_of_locallyOfFinitePresentation {S : Scheme.{u}} {X Y : AlgebraicSpace S} (f : X ⟶ Y) [HasDerivedCategory.{w} X.SmallModules] (hY : ∃ V : Y.EtaleSite, IsSurjective V.obj.hom ∧ IsLocallyNoetherian (Y.etaleForget.obj V)) (hf : MapIsLocallyOfFinitePresentation f) : (∃ U : X.EtaleSite, IsSurjective U.obj.hom ∧ IsLocallyNoetherian (X.etaleForget.obj U)) ∧ (SheafOfModules.unit X.smallStructureRings).IsFinitePresentation ∧ (∀ n : ℤ, ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor X.SmallModules n).obj (naiveCotangent f)).IsFinitePresentation) ∧ (∀ n : ℤ, n ≠ -1 → n ≠ 0 → IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor X.SmallModules n).obj (naiveCotangent f))) ∧ (∀ K : X.DerivedModules, K = naiveCotangent f ∨ K = X.derivedStructure → (∀ n : ℤ, ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor X.SmallModules n).obj K).IsFinitePresentation) ∧ ∃ a b : ℤ, ∀ n : ℤ, n < a ∨ b < n → IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor X.SmallModules n).obj K))
lean.note: Coherence is the existing small-site finite-presentation predicate, equivalent over locally Noetherian spaces to the stipulated finite-module association on every Noetherian affine etale chart (Stacks 07UB). The final conjunct unfolds bounded coherent cohomology for each of the two named derived objects, without introducing a duplicate category.
